title: U.S. House · Ohio's 13th District
area: Northeast Ohio, including Akron, Summit County and part of Stark County.

context.text: Incumbent Emilia Sykes (D) advanced unopposed from the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary. Carey Coleman won a five-way Republican primary. Sandeep Dixit is running as an independent and declared his candidacy for the general election.

summary.text: Emilia Sykes is the Democratic incumbent in Ohio's 13th Congressional District, which she has represented since January 2023. An Akron native and attorney, she served eight years in the Ohio House, including as House Minority Leader, before winning her congressional seat in 2022. She sits on the Transportation and Infrastructure and Science, Space, and Technology committees.

background.text: Born January 4, 1986, in Akron, Ohio, where she was raised; graduated from Firestone High School. She is the daughter of Vernon and Barbara Sykes, who held the same Ohio House seat before her.
Earned a bachelor's degree in psychology from Kent State University (graduating with honors), and a Juris Doctor and a Master of Public Health from the University of Florida.
Worked as a law clerk to the chief judge of the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of Georgia and as an administrative advisor in the Summit County fiscal office.

Won the Ohio House (34th District) seat in 2014, taking office in January 2015, to succeed her father, who was term-limited, after winning the Democratic primary over Summit County councilman Frank Communale.
Served eight years in the Ohio House, including four years in Democratic leadership and three as House Minority Leader, according to her official biography.
Won the November 2022 general election for Ohio's 13th District over Republican Madison Gesiotto Gilbert, and was re-elected in 2024 over Republican Kevin Coughlin, 51.1% to 48.9%.
In Congress she serves on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, where she is Vice Ranking Member, and on the Science, Space, and Technology Committee.

Her official biography lists recognitions including the Rising Star Award from EMILY's List and the Champion for Children Award from Summit County Children's Services, and states she is married to Kevin Boyce.

positions.summary: Supported Ohio Issue 1 (2023), the ballot measure establishing a state constitutional right to make reproductive decisions including abortion.
Her official site says she is working to expand access to Medicaid and Medicare and that healthcare is a human right.
positions.quote: She is working to lower the cost of prescription drugs, expand access to Medicaid and Medicare, and combat health disparities in our communities.

positions.summary: Her official site says she supports building clean energy infrastructure and domestic clean energy such as solar, wind, hydro, geothermal and biomass, with workforce programs for the transition.
positions.quote: Congresswoman Sykes supports policies that will save Ohioans money on their energy bills, create good-paying jobs, combat the climate crisis, and build a clean energy infrastructure that will support and bolster our economy.

positions.summary: In a Signal Akron questionnaire answer, said she voted for a War Powers Resolution directing the President to withdraw U.S. forces from the war in Iran, which she said was started without congressional authorization.
positions.quote: I voted to support a War Powers Resolution directing President Trump to withdraw our armed forces from the war in Iran, which he started without Congressional authorization,

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, including its Research and Technology Subcommittee (2023-2024).

Supported Ohio Issue 1 (2023) establishing a state constitutional right to abortion, which voters approved, and opposed the August 2023 measure that would have raised the vote threshold to approve future constitutional amendments to 60%, which voters rejected.

candidates.name: Carey Coleman

summary.text: Carey Coleman is the Republican nominee in Ohio's 13th Congressional District and a Northeast Ohio broadcaster. According to his campaign website, he has been a longtime radio host on WNIR and a television meteorologist, and he is running on fiscal discipline, secure borders and support for law enforcement.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he is a longtime Northeast Ohio radio host and community leader, known for commentary on WNIR.
According to his campaign website, he served for decades as a television meteorologist on national, statewide and local Northeast Ohio outlets.
Won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary for Ohio's 13th District with 47.3% of the vote, ahead of Kevin Siembida, Margaret Briem, Neil Patel and Sanjin Drakovac.
His campaign website says he lives in Northeast Ohio and is involved in local civic life and charitable causes; his campaign committee lists a Macedonia, Ohio, address.

priorities.text: Campaign site lists lowering the cost of living, including reining in federal spending and increasing energy production.
priorities.quote: He supports reining in out-of-control federal spending, restoring fiscal discipline, and ending wasteful programs that drive inflation.

priorities.text: Campaign site lists public safety and support for law enforcement, including stronger penalties for violent and repeat offenders.
Campaign site lists defending constitutional freedoms and limiting federal government power.
Campaign site lists job growth, workforce training and reshoring manufacturing.

positions.summary: Campaign site says he will advocate for increased resources for local police and federal help with recruiting, training and retaining officers.
positions.quote: He will advocate for increased resources for local police, stronger penalties for violent and repeat offenders, and federal partnerships that help local departments recruit, train, and retain quality officers.

candidates.researchNotes: From his campaign website issue pages only. He has not completed the Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and no debate or questionnaire coverage was found. The site's statements on border security, the Second Amendment and tariffs did not take a side on the guide's issue statements and were left out.

candidates.name: Sandeep Dixit

summary.text: Sandeep Dixit is an independent candidate in Ohio's 13th Congressional District. An engineer who came to the United States at age 21, he co-founded a software firm in 1996 and has been active in Mayfield Village community groups and Indian-American organizations. He describes his campaign as built around reason, work and freedom.

background.text: Immigrated to the United States at age 21, according to his survey response; he earned a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1989.

Earned a master's in integrated manufacturing systems engineering from North Carolina State University (1991, per his survey response; Ballotpedia's biography lists 1992) and an MBA from Cleveland State University, completed through evening and weekend classes while working full time.
Began as a shop-floor process engineer and moved to the Cleveland region in 1994; he and his wife started a software firm in 1996.

Active locally as a member of a Community Emergency Response Team (CERT), a board member of the Mayfield Village Parks and Recreation Department, and organizer of the Mayfield Village Yoga Festival since 2018.

Previously served as president of a national Indian-American organization with more than 500,000 members across 60 communities, according to his survey response; American Bazaar also reports leadership roles in Indian-American organizations.
Running without a major-party affiliation; American Bazaar reports his campaign centers on reason, work and freedom, with an emphasis on workforce development and fiscal responsibility.

priorities.text: Proposes $500 million per congressional district in vocational training investment.
Proposes a basic health-care guarantee for working people.
Proposes eliminating taxes on Social Security benefits.

positions.summary: Lists a 'basic healthcare guarantee for working people' as one of his three key campaign messages.
Campaign site lists raising the minimum wage among his key actions on good jobs.
positions.quote: Raise the minimum wage so full-time work makes living affordable.

candidates.researchNotes: From his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (2026) and campaign website issue page. The environment and privacy plan (enforcement of environmental regulations) did not take a side on a guide issue statement and was left out.

researchNotes: Carey Coleman has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; his biography here draws on his campaign website, and his birthplace, education and family are not published in the sources reviewed. Sandeep Dixit completed the survey, but his priorities and positions have not yet been added to this guide. Sources disagree on the year of Dixit's North Carolina State degree (1991 in his survey response, 1992 in Ballotpedia's biography). Federal key votes and FEC finance totals for Sykes are added separately.
